## 📖 About DRUZZ X-MD

**DRUZZ X-MD** is a **free, open-source WhatsApp Multi-Device bot** built for reliability, modularity, and easy deployment. It ships with a clean command system and a modular structure that makes it simple to extend, configure, and self-host — whether locally or on the cloud.

**Steps to fork:**

1. Open the GitHub repository using the GitHub icon in the navigation above.
2. Click the **Fork** button on the repository page.
3. Select your own GitHub account as the destination.
4. Wait for GitHub to finish creating your fork.
5. Open your newly created fork.
6. ⭐ Star the original repository to support the project.

---

## 📥 Clone

Clone the project to your local machine:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DruzzLabs/Druzz-x-md.git
cd Druzz-x-md
npm install
```

---

## 🛠️ Installation

Make sure you have **Node.js** installed, then run:

```bash
npm install
```

This installs all required dependencies defined in `package.json`.

---

## ⚙️ Configuration

DRUZZ X-MD is configured using environment variables.

1. If a `.env.example` file exists in the project, copy it:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

2. Open `.env` and fill in the values required by the project.

3. Save the file before starting the bot.

> ⚠️ **Security Notice:** Never publish, commit, or share your `.env` file, session files, tokens, passwords, or API keys publicly. Treat all credentials as private and confidential.

---

## ▶️ Local Run

After installing dependencies and configuring your environment file, start the bot:

```bash
npm start
```

Follow the on-screen instructions to link/authenticate your WhatsApp session.

**Deployment steps:**

1. Fork this repository (see the Fork section above).
2. Open Railway using the button above.
3. Log in to Railway with your GitHub account.
4. Create a **New Project**.
5. Choose **Deploy from GitHub Repo**.
6. Select your forked repository.
7. Configure the required environment variables in the Railway dashboard.
8. Start the deployment.
9. Open the deployment logs to monitor the build.
10. Verify the bot connects and is running successfully.

## 🩺 Troubleshooting

<table>
<tr><th align="left">Issue</th><th align="left">Possible Fix</th></tr>
<tr><td><code>npm install</code> errors</td><td>Ensure Node.js is installed and up to date, delete <code>node_modules</code> and <code>package-lock.json</code>, then reinstall.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Railway build errors</td><td>Check the deployment logs on Railway, confirm your <code>package.json</code> scripts are correct, and that all dependencies are listed.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Missing environment variables</td><td>Double check your <code>.env</code> file contains every variable required by the project, based on <code>.env.example</code>.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bot disconnecting</td><td>Ensure a stable internet/hosting connection and that your WhatsApp session hasn't been logged out from your phone.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Authentication problems</td><td>Delete the existing session data and re-authenticate/re-link your WhatsApp account.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Invalid configuration</td><td>Recheck your <code>.env</code> values for typos, missing quotes, or incorrect formatting.</td></tr>
</table>
